audiences.role: Bride or groom finalising vendors for a 200-400 guest Jakarta reception
audiences.jobToBeDone: Lock a photobooth vendor who will definitely show up, fit the venue, and not blow a budget that is already committed elsewhere.
painPoints: Every vendor hides pricing behind a WhatsApp chat, so comparing three of them takes a week
No idea whether the quoted duration covers setup and teardown or only live hours
Venue has loading restrictions nobody warned them about
objections: The advertised price is never the final price once backdrop and extra prints are added
Cannot tell whether this vendor has actually worked at their specific gedung
Afraid the booth will look cheap in the photos that end up on Instagram
audiences.decisionTrigger: Seeing a real total for a package matching their guest count and hours, from a vendor who has visibly worked that venue before.

audiences.role: EO or wedding organiser sourcing a repeatable vendor across multiple client events
audiences.jobToBeDone: Find one photobooth partner reliable enough to recommend to clients without personally supervising every setup.
painPoints: Vendors who cover Jakarta Selatan quietly refuse Jakarta Utara on the day
Operator quality varies event to event even with the same vendor
Needs a price list they can mark up and hand to a client in one message
objections: Cannot risk a no-show on a client event; reputation is the whole business
Needs proof of coverage across regions, not a claim
Wants to know operator count and backup equipment policy before recommending
audiences.decisionTrigger: A published coverage map plus a clear escalation and backup policy they can forward to a client verbatim.

audiences.role: Marketing lead running a mall or corporate activation in Jakarta
audiences.jobToBeDone: Commission a custom-branded booth that produces shareable output and captures leads at a mall or office event.
painPoints: Standard booth aesthetics clash with brand guidelines
Needs data capture, not just prints
objections: Most consumer photobooth vendors cannot handle brand guideline compliance
Unclear whether custom backdrop cost is one-off or per-event
No evidence of prior work with comparable brands
audiences.decisionTrigger: A custom-build portfolio with itemised costs and a named example of a comparable brand activation.

funnelMap.goal: Convert price-checking searchers directly into enquiries by being the only page that actually publishes numbers.
funnelMap.contentFormat: Transparent pricing page with package table and an interactive estimate
funnelMap.whyThisFormat: Every competitor forces a WhatsApp chat to reveal a price, so publishing one is both the differentiator and the conversion mechanism.

funnelMap.goal: Capture region-qualified demand and remove coverage doubt before the first message.
funnelMap.contentFormat: Coverage hub with a page per Jakarta region
funnelMap.whyThisFormat: All five regions autocomplete independently, which means searchers self-segment by area before they ever compare vendors.

funnelMap.goal: Help undecided searchers pick a booth format, and make our format the obvious fit for their event type.
funnelMap.contentFormat: Comparison guide with side-by-side format breakdown and real output samples
funnelMap.whyThisFormat: Format names are carrying the evaluation load here, and nobody explains them in terms of what a guest actually experiences.

funnelMap.goal: Monitor only. These searchers want a named operator and will not be converted by category content.
funnelMap.contentFormat: No dedicated content - track as a competitor watchlist
funnelMap.whyThisFormat: Building pages against branded navigational queries we do not own wastes production slots and rarely ranks.

contentGoals.primary: Turn price-stage searchers into qualified enquiries without forcing a chat first
contentGoals.secondary: Establish regional coverage as a defensible trust signal against single-area vendors
contentGoals.successMetric: Enquiries that arrive already naming a package and a region, as a share of total enquiries

portfolioAdvice: Build the pricing page first - it serves the largest and most commercially advanced cluster, and it is the only asset that attacks the market's shared weakness. The regional coverage hub is second because it compounds: every region page reinforces the pricing page's authority and captures demand the map pack currently absorbs. The format comparison guide is third; it is cheap and useful but it serves people who have not yet decided to spend. Cluster 4 gets nothing.
plannerNote: The entire Jakarta photobooth market has agreed, apparently by accident, to hide its prices. That is not a moat - it is a shared vulnerability, and the first vendor to publish a real number takes the whole bottom of the funnel.
